findings.reason: a §26 worker will find a landed case red under its own required behaviour and must either weaken a §6 requirement the plan never authorises changing or drop the fourth deliverable, so the plan needs to state whether §6's no-owner case is superseded (and renamed to the no-session case) or whether the new naming is scoped to a path that leaves the shim's rule intact.
findings.text: §26's fourth deliverable ("a job reckon submits for a coordinator session with no run id names that session") contradicts the landed §6 case `test_a_submission_outside_any_run_adds_nothing` at `tests/test_a_scheduler_job_names_its_owner.py:163`, which submits with `session=SESSION, run=None` — a coordinator session with no run id — and asserts the comment is `None`; both go through `nested_launch.owner_comment`, which returns `""` whenever `RECKON_RUN_ID` is absent, so the file cannot be green under both expectations without the plan saying which one changes

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the cited test modules `tests/test_a_scheduler_job_names_its_owner.py`, `tests/test_a_landed_head_is_not_landed_again.py` and `tests/test_worker_behaviour_is_the_same_on_every_harness.py` all exist, §16 resolves as a section, and §27's run id is given in full rather than truncated.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §26's done-when cannot be satisfied as written: its fourth deliverable requires the shim to name a session when no run id is present, and the landed §6 case `tests/test_a_scheduler_job_names_its_owner.py:169` submits that exact shape and asserts no comment.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every changed section's evidence is a test under `tests/` plus the run record's own gate log; no session scratchpad or node-local temporary path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test filenames and the described behaviours are named by mechanism (`test_a_launch_records_its_nodes_role.py`, `test_a_resumed_launch_keeps_its_lane.py`, `test_a_message_reaches_a_seeded_inbox.py`), with no plan label, ticket number or version tag carried into a symbol or a file name.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — each stated root cause was checked against the tree and holds: `behaviour_role` defaults to `implement` at `reckon/_backends.py:3192` with no production caller passing it (§25); the existing §6 cases all hand `RECKON_SESSION_ID` in themselves at `tests/test_a_scheduler_job_names_its_owner.py:104` (§26); `_backend_settings` rebuilds from a short field list with no `lane_document` and is called with `config=None` on the plain resume path at `reckon/crew/resumption.py:939` (§28); `crew_tell` still branches on the dialect name at `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2982` (§29); and the equality test composes with `fence=False` at `tests/test_worker_behaviour_is_the_same_on_every_harness.py:48`, which does make the protections and write roots empty by construction (§30).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §25 now carries only the recorded role; §26's four deliverables are one capability (the scheduler job comment's owner provenance on one surface proven through four shapes); §27, §28, §29 and §30 each name one deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the declared waits (`s3`→`s2`, `s4`→`s2`,`s5`, `s5`→`s2`, `s16`→`s12`) all resolve to sections that exist, the followup `f-wlsr-001` restates exactly those waits, and §28, §29 and §30 name no dependency because the upstream they build on (§16) is declared done and has landed.
